canonical_title: JPMorgan-backed Alliance for Critical Infrastructure expands into cross-industry AI risk coordination
aliases: Alliance for Critical Infrastructure AI risks
Jamie Dimon AI critical infrastructure coalition
treatment: Treat as private-sector critical-infrastructure coordination around AI and cyber risk. Reinclude only for named membership expansion, formal standards or safeguards, concrete incident-sharing mechanisms, government agreements, published technical guidance, or operational launch milestones.
known_facts: Reuters reported that JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon is expanding the Alliance for Critical Infrastructure's focus to include AI risks.
Outreach includes more than 40 companies across financial services, energy, water, utilities, telecommunications, airlines, railroads and other critical-infrastructure sectors.
The initiative aims to build a shared understanding of AI use, risks and safeguards and to coordinate with the U.S. government.
The ACI is intended to function as an industry response and information-sharing forum for AI and technology risks.
Reuters reported that the revamped ACI aims to be fully functional by the end of 2026.
This effort is distinct from separate bank testing of Anthropic's Mythos models and from the U.S. government's Gold Eagle initiative.
reinclude_only_if: ACI publishes formal AI safeguards, technical guidance, standards, incident-sharing rules, or response playbooks.
Major new members or named AI developers formally join the initiative.
ACI enters a concrete agreement with federal agencies or the White House on AI risk coordination.
The group becomes operational and discloses material findings, incidents, or remediation mechanisms.
notes: Selected because it creates a new cross-sector operational coordination layer for AI risk in critical infrastructure rather than merely adding commentary to existing government testing stories.
